title: Male borrowers who mention specific geographic locations may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who mention the loan amount in local currency may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who mention their age and education level may fund faster.
Mentioning marital status or children without specifying benefits may slow funding for women.
Male borrowers who include specific details about personal background or secondary income may fund faster.
Female borrowers who provide detailed counts of children may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who mention long-term infrastructure goals, such as building a house or stall, may fund more slowly.
Detailed lists of inventory or ingredients in retail/food pitches may slow funding for women.
Mentioning biographical details such as education level or daily routines predicts slower funding regardless of gender.
Detailed and lengthier pitches may accelerate funding for female borrowers.
Mentioning specific institutional or brand names predicts slower funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who list specific products or goals beyond family welfare fund faster.
Explicit expressions of gratitude to lenders accelerate funding for female borrowers.
Female borrowers who mention benefits to their family or community fund faster.
Mentioning benefits for children predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Specifying the number of years a business has operated predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Longer pitch text predicts slower funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who mention their husband's role or family structure fund faster.
